description: Flat 8 m square of rounded cobblestone setts bedded in sand -- one quad, one seamless PBR texture set, tiling in both axes.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of old cobblestone paving seen as a single unbroken surface, densely packed rounded stone setts of slightly varying size and tone bedded tight against each other with narrow sandy joints, edge to edge stone only, no kerb and no border Materials: Seamlessly tiling weathered grey and warm brown granite setts, tops worn smooth and faintly polished where traffic runs, rougher pitted flanks, pale sand and grit packed into the narrow joints with moss creeping through in the damper runs, a few sunken and a few tilted stones, thin dust film and dark damp patches; the stone layout must wrap on all four edges so any edge meets any other edge with no visible join or repeated stone at the seam.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Cobblestone Paving Tile
nameTh: พื้นหินก้อน
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; not a single stone is modelled, and the bumps underfoot are the normal and AO maps doing all the work. This is a member of the kit's ground-surface tile set: every tile in that set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so any ground tile butts flush against any other and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside them as a separate object. Because cobble layout is irregular with no course direction, this tile is fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric -- it drops in at any of four orientations, which is what stops a large paved area reading as an obvious grid of copies. Seamlessness is the one hard requirement: the stone layout has to wrap on all four edges, and the thing to check first on the generated texture is that no distinctive stone appears twice across a seam, which is the failure that makes a repeat visible from across a square. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end tiling PBR texture set and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. Cobblestone is not common on Thai streets -- it belongs to restored old-town lanes, hotel forecourts, riverside promenades and garden paths -- so this is a set-dressing surface rather than a default ground, and the kit's everyday paving is the interlocking concrete paver. It is distinct from the Pebble-Wash Terrazzo Paving Tile, which is small pebbles set FLUSH in cement panels with visible divider strips; these are chunky proud stones with open joints. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable.
